skill.name: fiftyone-code-style
skill.description: Apply FiftyOne Python conventions for imports, docstrings, utility reuse, error handling, validation, and plugin-friendly code structure.
skill.summary: Guides Python code toward FiftyOne project conventions for imports, docstrings, utilities, lazy imports, and validation.

content.value_statement: FiftyOne contributors need consistent Python style across imports, docstrings, utilities, and validation. This skill provides focused conventions and checklists for compatible code.
actual_capabilities: Provides a module template with header docstring, imports, logger setup, public functions, and private helpers.
Defines FiftyOne import groups and common aliases for core modules and utilities.
Shows Google-style docstring patterns for functions, classes, arguments, returns, and raised errors.
Recommends lazy imports, optional dependency guards, and non-fatal warning patterns.
Includes a checklist for style compliance, quality checks, linting, formatting, and tests.
Directs users to reuse FiftyOne and eta utilities before adding redundant implementations.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run formatting, linting, or tests by itself.
It focuses on FiftyOne Python conventions, not general style for every Python project.
It does not replace project maintainers, CI rules, or code review requirements.
It does not validate whether referenced FiftyOne APIs are available in every installed version.

use_cases.title: Prepare FiftyOne Contributions
use_cases.description: Align new modules, imports, docstrings, and helper functions with FiftyOne repository conventions before submitting a pull request.

use_cases.title: Build Consistent Plugins
use_cases.description: Use the documented aliases, lazy import guidance, and validation checklist when writing FiftyOne plugin code.

use_cases.title: Review Python Changes
use_cases.description: Compare proposed code against a compact checklist for import ordering, utility reuse, docstrings, logging, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Format A Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single Python file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python module for FiftyOne code style. Focus on import groups, aliases, module layout, logger setup, and private helper naming.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Docstrings
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite these docstrings in the FiftyOne Google-style pattern. Include Args, Returns, and Raises sections only where they apply.

prompt_templates.title: Check Utility Reuse
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this implementation for redundant helpers. Suggest existing FiftyOne or eta utilities that may replace custom path, JSON, image, or type-checking logic.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a FiftyOne style pass on this change. Check import organization, lazy imports, guard patterns, warning behavior, utility reuse, tests, and lint commands.

output_examples.input: A new FiftyOne module with mixed import order and missing logger setup.
output: Move standard library imports before third-party, eta, and FiftyOne imports.
Add module-level logger setup after imports.
Use the documented FiftyOne aliases for core modules.

output_examples.input: A function with informal comments instead of a public API docstring.
output: Use a Google-style docstring with a short summary.
Add Args entries for each parameter and include defaults where useful.
Add Returns and Raises sections only when the function behavior requires them.

output_examples.input: A plugin change that imports a heavy optional dependency at module load time.
output: Use lazy import guidance for optional or heavy dependencies.
Add a clear fallback or warning path for missing optional packages.
Confirm the validation checklist covers linting, formatting, and targeted tests.

best_practices: Use the import group order before making deeper style changes.
Check existing FiftyOne and eta utilities before creating new helper functions.
Run linting, formatting checks, and targeted tests after applying the guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the examples as a complete replacement for repository CI.
Do not add heavy imports at module load time when lazy imports are appropriate.
Do not create duplicate utilities without checking FiftyOne and eta modules first.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps write and review Python code that follows FiftyOne project conventions.

faq.question: Does it modify files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, review points, and suggested changes for an AI coding assistant to apply.

faq.question: Can I use it for FiftyOne plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers plugin-friendly patterns such as import aliases, lazy imports, warnings, and validation checks.

faq.question: Does it run pylint, black, or pytest?
faq.answer: No. It lists validation commands, but the user or coding agent must run them separately.

faq.question: Is it useful outside FiftyOne?
faq.answer: Some Python style guidance is general, but the aliases and utility recommendations are specific to FiftyOne.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
